steps.title: Calculate a mixture average
steps.content: When quantities with different prices or concentrations are mixed, the mean value is the weighted average: total value divided by total quantity.
steps.example: Mix 2 kg at ₹40/kg with 3 kg at ₹60/kg. Mean price = (80+180)/5 = ₹52/kg.

steps.title: Find a weighted average
steps.prompt: 20 kg of rice at ₹80/kg is mixed with 30 kg at ₹100/kg. Find the average price.
steps.explanation: Total cost = 20×80 + 30×100 = ₹4,600. Total weight = 50 kg. Mean price = ₹92/kg.

steps.title: Use the alligation rule
steps.content: When mixing a lower value L and a higher value H to obtain mean M, the ratio of lower-value quantity to higher-value quantity is (H−M):(M−L).
steps.formula: Quantity at L : Quantity at H = (H−M) : (M−L)
steps.example: Mix 40% and 60% solutions for a 50% solution: ratio = (60−50):(50−40) = 1:1.

steps.title: Apply alligation
steps.prompt: In what ratio should 20% and 50% solutions be mixed to obtain 30%?

steps.title: Replacing part of a mixture
steps.content: If a vessel is well mixed and a fraction is removed and replaced with water, the original ingredient is reduced by the same fraction each time. Repeat the multiplication for repeated replacements.
steps.example: Remove 1/4 of a 40 L mixture: 30 L of the original mixture remains before replacement.

questions.prompt: 10 kg at ₹20/kg is mixed with 10 kg at ₹40/kg. What is the average price?
Mix 30% and 60% solutions to obtain 50%. What is the lower:higher quantity ratio?
A 40 L mixture is 25% water. How much water does it contain?
Mix 20% and 40% solutions equally. What is the resulting concentration?
questions.explanation: Equal quantities give the mean concentration (20+40)/2 = 30%.

questions.prompt: Which method is best for mixing two prices to obtain a target mean price?
questions.explanation: Alligation directly gives the ratio of quantities needed for a target mean.
